deltas.description: The unique-minimum assertion is expressed by the equivalent nonnegativity, value-at-origin and exact-zero-set conditions.
deltas.evidence: For real-valued f these conditions are logically equivalent to the source assertion; the definition is the actual quadratic potential, not an abstract supplied function.
deltas.reconstructed: Value 0 at 0, nonnegativity everywhere, and zero iff the vector is 0.

review_evidence: Independently read the full original Lemma B.8 proof, including its final strict-positivity argument, and compared the packet current Lean proof with every English lesson step. The proof simplifies the actual potential at 0, obtains hlow from blockPrecision_regular with the same hn,hnd,hκ and O, and proves coordinate-square nonnegativity. If energy is zero, hlow forces x dot x=0. Finset.single_le_sum then makes each coordinate square zero and mul_self_eq_zero gives x=0; the reverse direction simplifies at 0. These proof steps establish exactly the lesson statement and the equivalent unique-minimum conclusion. No positivity or zero-set estimate is taken as a producer hypothesis. This is a scoped independent semantic review of the supplied candidate only. Compilation and axiom reports were supplied as background and are not used as semantic equivalence evidence; no aggregate-gate outcome is asserted.

assumptions.evidence: Pinned section 3.1 states these bounds before (4),(5). Lemma 3.4 and full Appendix B.3 apply to every orthogonal tuple. The theorem has no common determinant-sign, random-law, query-budget, or pre-established spectral-estimate hypothesis. hnd is retained even where not needed internally.
assumptions.original: The standing construction fixes kappa>=4 and 3<=n<=d, with orthogonal blocks; regularity itself is deterministic.
assumptions.reconstructed: Explicit hn : 3<=n, hnd : n<=d, hκ : 4<=kappa, and each block typed as an orthogonal matrix.

conclusion.evidence: Nonnegativity plus f(0)=0 says 0 is a global minimum with value 0. The iff makes its zero level set exactly {0}, so every minimizer is 0; over R it also gives strict positivity at every nonzero x. Conversely unique minimum at 0 with value 0 implies nonnegativity and this iff. Thus no uniqueness or minimum-value clause is weakened.
conclusion.original: f_A(x)=(1/2)x^T A x has unique minimizer 0 and minimum value 0; the source proof gives strict positivity for x!=0.
conclusion.reconstructed: For this exact potential, f(0)=0 and every x satisfies 0<=f(x) and (f(x)=0 iff x=0).

constant_dependencies.evidence: There are no hidden existential constants or dimension-dependent losses. The tail estimate uses only 1<=kappa, derived from the retained 4<=kappa. The minimum proof multiplies by exactly the positive scalar 1/2.
constant_dependencies.original: The literal block coefficients are (kappa+1)/2 and (kappa-1)/4; bounds use exactly 1 and kappa.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The expanded expression has those same coefficients, with quotient/remainder determined solely by d,n.

domains.evidence: The real orthogonal group is the full group, including either determinant sign. Fin-indexed functions represent tuples and Euclidean vectors. Nat quotient equals floor(d/n) in the source standing range; Nat.div_add_mod identifies d%n with d-(d/n)*n.
domains.original: 3<=n<=d natural dimensions, real kappa>=4, all O in O(n)^floor(d/n), vectors in R^d.
domains.reconstructed: Natural d,n with 3<=n and n<=d; real kappa with 4<=kappa; O : Fin(d/n) -> orthogonalGroup(Fin n) R; x : Fin d -> R.

objects.evidence: Pinned section 3.1 equations (4),(5); the packet expands singleBlockPrecision to exactly equation (4). prodComm followed by finProdFinEquiv flattens (i,j) as j*n+i; sum flattening places tail t at (d/n)*n+t. Reindex uses the inverse of this same equivalence on both matrix indices. Thus the matrix is the literal consecutive-block precision, not an arbitrary permutation or abstract surrogate.
objects.original: Real orthogonal n by n blocks A_O=((kappa+1)/2)I-((kappa-1)/4)(O+O^T), in a d-dimensional block precision.
objects.reconstructed: Fin(d/n)-indexed orthogonalGroup(Fin n) blocks with the same expanded entries, followed by an identity on Fin(d%n), reindexed to Fin d.

quantifiers.evidence: The binders preserve dependence: d,n determine the tuple size; kappa and that tuple determine A. No vector-dependent choice of A or tuple is introduced.
quantifiers.original: For every admissible orthogonal tuple; regularity and the minimum assertion hold for every vector.
quantifiers.reconstructed: d,n,kappa and O are universally quantified; x is universally quantified inside the theorem for the same literal A.
